blogs.title: From Text Prompts to Photorealism: A Beginner’s Guide to Text‑to‑Image Diffusion Models
blogs.description: An accessible overview of how modern diffusion models turn words into high‑quality images, why they’re considered breakthroughs in AI art, and what challenges arise when you try to steer them for specific tasks such as personalized or controlled image generation.

blogs.title: Why Angles Matter More Than Lengths: The Core Idea Behind Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT)
blogs.description: Explains the intuition behind hyperspherical energy and how preserving the pairwise angles between neurons keeps a model’s semantic knowledge intact. The post breaks down the math into visual analogies (e.g., rotating vectors on a sphere) and shows why an orthogonal transformation is a “sweet spot” for stable finetuning.

blogs.title: DreamBooth Reimagined: How OFT Improves Subject‑Driven Image Generation
blogs.description: Discusses the classic DreamBooth approach for generating images of a specific subject from just a few photos, then shows how Orthogonal Finetuning (and its constrained variant COFT) boost identity preservation, converge faster, and need fewer training steps. Includes side‑by‑side examples and simple charts that illustrate the performance gains.

blogs.title: Controlling Images with Canny Edges, Segmentation Maps, and More – OFT’s Take on Controllable Generation
blogs.description: Walks readers through three popular control signals—edge sketches, semantic masks, and facial landmarks—and demonstrates how OFT outperforms ControlNet, T2I‑Adapter, and LoRA in both speed and quality. Introduces the new “control consistency” metric in plain language and explains why it matters.

blogs.title: Under the Hood: Efficient Orthogonal Parameterization & the COFT Extension
blogs.description: Dives into the engineering tricks that make OFT practical at scale—Cayley transforms, block‑diagonal orthogonal matrices, and the epsilon‑radius constraint of Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning. The post uses step‑by‑step diagrams to show how these techniques keep training fast while respecting the model’s original knowledge.

blogs.title: OFT vs. LoRA vs. ControlNet: A Head‑to‑Head Comparison for Practitioners
blogs.description: Provides an easy‑to‑read comparison table and narrative that highlights key differences in parameter efficiency, inference overhead, convergence speed, and final image fidelity among Orthogonal Finetuning, LoRA’s low‑rank updates, and adapter‑based methods like ControlNet.

blogs.title: Future Directions: Scaling Orthogonal Finetuning and Compositional Control
blogs.description: Looks ahead at open problems identified by the authors—speeding up matrix inverses in Cayley transforms, stacking multiple orthogonal adapters for compositional tasks, and improving parameter efficiency beyond block‑diagonal structures—while suggesting concrete research ideas for curious readers.
